answer: Each applicant gets a numbered glass prism by mail, etched with a pattern no two share. The applicant carries it to a tundra station for a warden to photograph its split light on a white card. At another station a second warden repeats the shot to match the registry. A hollow copy fails, since empty glass throws a flat spot. Fee 120 dollars, bond 150 tokens; a mismatch forfeits the bond and bars the applicant 180 days. Forging 10,000 identities costs 1,200,000 dollars and 1,500,000 frozen tokens. A prism is a key that only works in the hand that carried it, so a faker walks the tundra.
